Sam H: Hey team — MerchantPay (Maya) just asked for a prompt inventory and a baseline prompt engineering plan so we can finalize POC scope. Can we list what we need to deliver this week?
Priya K: Short checklist: 1) full prompt inventory (happy path + edge cases), 2) baseline prompt set for evals, 3) success metrics, 4) timeline + token budget, 5) any security/data constraints.
Ethan L: Also need expected concurrent sessions and avg sequence lengths so we can estimate token throughput. Maya, can you share typical session examples?
Maya (MerchantPay): Most sessions are short — 2–4 turns, ~200 tokens per session avg. A few reconciliation flows hit ~900 tokens. We can pull 150 redacted examples for test set.
Jo S: Security note: MerchantPay requires that any customer data used in evals be redacted and handled in Private deployment or Dedicated with BYOK. They asked about SOC2 / encryption in transit + at rest.
Priya K: Got it. For the prompt inventory, structure like: use_case, sample_input, expected_output, failure_modes. Example prompts (baseline) below:
```
# Customer support summary
System: You are a payments assistant.
User: "Charge for order 123 failed, needs refund"
Assistant: "Summarize issue and next steps (one paragraph)."
```
```
# Reconciliation rule explanation
System: You are a payments engineer helper.
User: "Why did transaction 890 show mismatch?"
Assistant: "Explain likely causes and checks to run (bullet list)."
```
Ethan L: Baseline infra config suggestion: hosted API with quantized small-medium model for latency-sensitive flows, dedicated for high-throughput reconciliation. Targets: P95 latency < 400ms for 200-token paths, throughput 60 QPS for peak.
EvalBot: Suggested eval matrix: precision/recall or F1 for classification tasks, BLEU/ROUGE for summaries, end-to-end correctness rate for business rules. Minimum test set: 100 labeled items per use-case. A/B baseline: current human output vs model.
Sam H: Pricing question from Maya: what is rough incremental cost for running a 4-week POC with ~60 QPS bursts and 150 test records? Need an order of magnitude for procurement.
Ethan L: Order-of-magnitude: hosted API tokens + infra — expect ~$5k–$12k depending on model family and streaming. Dedicated reserve starts higher (monthly commit). I'll run a quick calc and post numbers.
Priya K: Success criteria proposal (vote): 1) Functional correctness >= 88% on test set, 2) Human acceptability >= 85% (subjective review), 3) P95 latency <= 400ms for customer-facing prompts, 4) No P0 security blockers (e.g., data leakage). Thoughts?
Maya (MerchantPay): Those look reasonable. We need explicit redaction steps. Also can we include a simple rollback playbook if quality regresses?
Jo S: Add to deliverables: redaction script, data handling doc, and a short SOC/compliance checklist.
Sam H: Timeline check: 1) Prompt inventory + sample prompts due by EOW (Fri), 2) Baseline eval harness + metrics next Wed, 3) POC starts Apr 5 for 4 weeks. Confirm?
Maya (MerchantPay): Confirmed on timeline. We'll deliver redacted samples by Thu.
Ethan L: I'll post an initial token budget estimate by EOD. Also attaching recommended model variants: gpt-small-q4_0, rwf-medium-qa. (We'll finalize after token calc).
Priya K: I'll draft the inventory template and drop it here in a thread reply. :thumbsup:
Sam H: Great — if everyone ok, I'll create the repo and invite MerchantPay to view the prompt inventory doc. :rocket:
EvalBot: Note: create eval labels as JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected, category, severity.
Priya K: (follow-up) template posted: https://redwood.internal/drive/merchantpay/prompt-inventory-template.xlsx
Maya (MerchantPay): Thanks all — appreciate the clarity.
Sam H: Thanks team — keeping this thread as single source for POC prompt decisions. :white_check_mark:
